title: Dietitian Reviews The Dirty Dozen | Should You Buy Organic or Conventional Produce?
summary: Dietitian reviews the Dirty Dozen and organic produce, arguing residues are far below harmful levels, organic is no safer or more nutritious and uses more land, and fear-based lists discourage people from eating produce.

assertions.quote: certified to have grown on soil that had no prohibited substances applied for three years prior to harvest
this does not mean that organic produce is pesticide free
the amount of pesticides found on our food is far below the level that has been shown to be harmful
organic farming is often much less sustainable because it uses up more land than conventional farming
organic produce is no safer or no more nutritious than its conventional counterparts
when you choose organic it's often going to be way more expensive
the dirty dozen clean 15 is not dietitian approved it is just a scare tactic from a biased organization
lower income consumers are less likely to purchase any produce due to these misleading messages

verdicts.note: One survey experiment found low-income shoppers less willing to buy produce after residue messaging; real-world effects are unmeasured.

assertions.quote: any way that you can incorporate more fruits and vegetables is going to be great for you
if you are choosing to eat organic because it is better for the environment i challenge you to get curious
